title: Re-Create Yourself
coreMove: Refashion the public role before stale identity lets others manage you automatically
sourcePressure: Chapter 25 is supported here by the frozen title and grouped secondary summaries: power can involve deliberate self-fashioning rather than passive acceptance of a fixed identity. The mechanism should stay narrow. The chapter is about self-creation, image control, and refusing stale roles that make a person predictable or easily managed. Keep it grounded in crafted public form, strategic reinvention, and the limit that reinvention fails when it becomes hollow theater with no governing center underneath. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
